# AI-Rulez

> The standards-compliant lifecycle tool for agent knowledge and capabilities: author, generate, bundle, validate, govern, publish

## Docs

- [Home](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/): AI-Rulez is a standards-compliant lifecycle tool for agent knowledge and capabilities.

## Get started

- [Installation](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/installation/): Install ai-rulez using your preferred package manager.
- [Quick Start](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/quick-start/): Get AI-Rulez running in 5 minutes.
- [Standards](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/standards/): ai-rulez claims conformance with a standard only when a passing test backs the claim.
- [Migrating to v5](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/migration-v5/): This page collects the breaking changes of the v5 release and what ai-rulez migrate v5 does about each.

## Author

- [Configuration](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/configuration/): Configuration reference for .ai-rulez/config.toml (YAML and JSON configs are no longer read; ai-rulez migrate v5 converts them).
- [Rules](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/rules/): Most AI tools can load rules from a folder, one file per rule, each with its own activation: always on, only when matching files are in play, only when the model finds the description relevant, or...
- [Skill Frontmatter](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/skills/): A skill is .ai-rulez/skills/\<id\>/SKILL.md: YAML frontmatter followed by the instructions.
- [Checks](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/checks/): Checks are code-review guidelines: per-topic instructions a review tool applies to a pull or merge request.
- [OKF (Open Knowledge Format)](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/okf/): ai-rulez can export its rules, context, skills, agents and commands as an OKF bundle, import an existing OKF bundle into .ai-rulez/, keep a bundle in sync through the opt-in okf preset, and lint...
- [Domains & Profiles](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/domains/): Organize AI configuration by team, subsystem, or project area.
- [Roles](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/roles/): A profile picks domains for a project.
- [Includes](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/includes/): Reuse configurations across multiple projects through inheritance and composition.
- [Installed Skills](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/installed-skills/): Install named skills from external repositories.
- [Local Configuration](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/local-overrides/): Personal, machine-local configuration that is never committed.
- [Catalog](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/catalog/): ai-rulez catalog describes everything a repository defines: rules, context, skills, agents, commands and checks, with owner, version, size, the digest ai-rulez.lock pins, the roles that keep each...
- [Monorepo](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/monorepo/): For large projects with multiple teams, organize your .ai-rulez/ configuration using domains and profiles to provide relevant context while avoiding overwhelming AI assistants with irrelevant...
- [Examples](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/examples/): ai-rulez uses a file-based directory structure (.ai-rulez/) with TOML configuration.

## Generate

- [Supported Harnesses](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/harnesses/): ai-rulez ships 52 built-in presets, one per AI coding harness.
- [AGENTS.md and .agents/skills](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/agents-md/): AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/ are the closest thing to a cross-tool convention for project instructions and Agent Skills.
- [llms.txt](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/llms-txt/): llms.txt is a markdown file at the root of a site or repository that tells language models what is there and where to read it.
- [Hooks and Permissions](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/settings/): ai-rulez generate can write the lifecycle hooks, permission rules and a few other settings keys of a project into each harness's native settings file, without shipping a plugin.
- [Permissions](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/permissions/): The top-level \[permissions\] block is one allow/ask/deny list for every harness that has a native permission surface.
- [User-level Configuration](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/user-scope/): ai-rulez generate writes inside the project.
- [Custom Presets](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/profiles/): Set presets in .ai-rulez/config.toml to control which tools ai-rulez generates for.
- [Baz](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/baz/): The baz preset writes what the Baz pull request reviewer reads from a repository.
- [Harness Traps](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/harness-traps/): Some harnesses accept a file that looks valid and then silently ignore it: a rule written to .cursor/rules/x.md is never read, and a Copilot path file named go.md is skipped.

## Bundle and publish

- [Authoring Plugins](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/plugins/): ai-rulez generate --plugin packages your .ai-rulez/ project into distributable plugin bundles and a marketplace index for the Claude, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Kimi, OpenCode, Factory, and Hermes...
- [Agent Plugins](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/agent-plugins/): ai-rulez packages a project's skills and MCP servers as an Agent Plugins plugin directory, so any client that conforms to the standard can load them.
- [Agentic Resource Discovery](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/ard/): ai-rulez can publish your skills, MCP servers and plugin for discovery through Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD): one ard.json manifest that a registry or an agent fetches from...
- [Publish](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/publish/): ai-rulez publish turns the generated plugin bundle into release artifacts: a reproducible tar.gz, a manifest, checksums and a plan.

## Validate

- [Strict Validation](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/strict-validation/): ai-rulez validate checks that configuration parses and matches the schema.
- [Verifiers](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/verifiers/): \[\[verifiers\]\] declares deterministic, read-only checks over the repository, run by ai-rulez verifiers run.
- [Poly Hooks](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/poly-hooks/): AI-Rulez publishes a reusable Poly hook catalog in poly-hooks.toml.

## Govern

- [Trust Model](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/trust-model/): A repository's .ai-rulez/ configuration is content someone else may have written: you clone it, run ai-rulez generate, and it should not be able to spend your money, send your data anywhere, or...
- [Lock File](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/lockfile/): ai-rulez.lock (in the configuration directory, committed) is the record of exactly what your AI configuration is made of.
- [Approvals](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/approvals/): A scan says content looks clean; an approval says a named person read it and accepted it.
- [Signing](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/signing/): A digest proves that bytes did not change.
- [Organization Policy](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/policy/): An organization policy is a floor a repository may raise but never lower.
- [SBOM](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/sbom/): ai-rulez sbom prints a bill of materials of the project's AI configuration as CycloneDX 1.6 or SPDX 2.3 JSON.
- [Forge Client](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/forge/): internal/forge is a small, read-only GitHub REST client.

## Operate

- [MCP Server](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/mcp-server/): The ai-rulez MCP (Model Context Protocol) server allows your AI assistant to programmatically and safely interact with your .ai-rulez/ configuration.
- [Item-Load Telemetry (OTLP)](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/telemetry/): Usage telemetry answers "which skills are ever invoked".
- [Usage Telemetry](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/usage-telemetry/): Which generated skills are ever used, which fire when they should not, and which can be retired?
- [Evals](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/evals/): ai-rulez gives eval cases a supported place to live, keeps them out of the context your agents load, ships them in plugin bundles when you ask, and can report skills that have none.
- [Improve (experimental)](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/improve/): ai-rulez improve run \<skill\> --with CMD runs an external optimizer (a tool that rewrites a skill against a benchmark) on a throwaway copy of the skill and accepts a candidate only if a held-out...
- [Skill Search](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/search/): ai-rulez search ranks the skills your project serves against a query, with the same ranker as the findskill tool of mcp --serve-skills, and measures that ranking against labeled queries.
- [Review](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/review/): ai-rulez review scores skills, agents and commands against a rubric you own.
- [LLM Access](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/llm/): internal/llm.Client is the one Go interface for reaching a language model, so the provider, the cost controls and the privacy rules live in one place.
- [Performance](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/performance/): How ai-rulez is benchmarked, how a regression is caught, and what the optimization passes changed.

## Reference

- [Standards](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/standards/): ai-rulez claims conformance with a standard only when a passing test backs the claim.
- [CLI Commands](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/cli/): All AI-Rulez CLI commands and flags.
- [Schema](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/schema/): The ai-rulez configuration is validated against a formal JSON Schema to provide editor support like autocompletion and real-time validation.
- [Embedding (Go API)](https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/embedding/): github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/v5/pkg/airulez loads a project, validates it, plans or applies a generate run and writes or checks its lock from Go, inside a process that may serve many projects at...
